:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width='60%'}
::: {style='font-size: 85%'}
1. Swap the nurse and specialist resources for `VidigiPriorityStore`, and pass `priority=patient.priority` into their `.request()` calls so higher-priority patients are seen first
1. Add `patient_priority` as a separate field on the logging steps [(it's not the same as the `priority` argument above - one controls the queue, the other is just for the log)]{style="color:lightgrey;font-size: 65%"}
1. Switch to using the three-step animation process
1. Customise the icons so that high-priority patients are displayed differently
1. Add a synchronised trace panel for each of the three queues (registration, nurse, specialist), showing each queue's length as a line that builds up over time [(see the *Adding Synchronised Traces* section for the technique - you'll need `add_subplot_panels` with more than one extra row, and one `add_synchronised_trace_from_dataframe` call per queue targeting a different axis pair; with more panels stacked up you'll also want to increase the overall plot height - try setting `plotly_height=1200` in your `generate_animation()` call)]{style="color:lightgrey;font-size: 65%"}
:::
:::

::: {.column width='40%'}
::: {.fragment}
::: {style='font-size: 70%; color: lightgrey'}
### Extensions
- Try creating separate process maps for each priority of patient.
- Try adding some additional information to your patients. What about their wait time, or something else you think would be useful to include? Could you swap the icons to represent something else and use text to display their priority?
- Create a custom background in draw.io (or your preferred software) and apply it to your animation.
- Instead of (or as well as) the line plots, try adding an animated bar chart showing how many patients are currently waiting in each queue, updating every frame. The [vidigi docs' "per-frame bar" example](https://hsma-tools.github.io/vidigi/examples/feat_synchronised_traces/#step-2---a-per-frame-bar-add_synchronised_trace_from_dataframe) shows the pattern you'll need - note it uses `go.Bar` and `accumulate=False` rather than the `go.Scatter`/`accumulate=True` line pattern from earlier.
:::
:::
:::
